card.name: Simdi
card.tagline: Stately Ossetian mass couple dance in black and white
card.profile: Simdi is an Ossetian-origin folk dance performed in Georgia by many couples, distinguished by long-sleeved costumes, exceptionally high headwear and the stark contrast of black and white attire (Wikipedia; Georgia About). Its beauty lies in strict graphic line formations, softness of movement and precise synchrony; stern-looking men stand beside the women as a protective, deferential presence. Derived from the verb 'simyn' ('mass dance'), a Simd can involve very large numbers of dancers; it traces back to the Alans and originally had ritual, sacred meaning connected with a sun cult and military training (hobbyblendfun). It is closely related to, but distinct from, the Ossetian invitation dance Khonga.
card.insight: Simdi was historically a courtship vehicle for young people forbidden to meet alone - the long sleeves and 'no-touching' rule enforced formal propriety - and survives as a celebration of classical purity and harmony among Georgia's Ossetian community (Georgia About).
card.image_significance: Stately long-sleeved gliding couples. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — Ossetian-origin, Georgia.
